verdict_reason: Ordinary-data arithmetic and aggregation are faithful: the current kernel matched a direct local execution of the released routine over 200 trajectories to max absolute error 4.44e-15. Two current-code counterexamples nevertheless fail the estimand. First, a nonzero right turn scaled to 1e-13 returns 0 angles because of the absolute 1e-12 cutoff, while the released routine returns 1.5707963705 rad. Second, evaluate() publishes a per-layer profile when requested final-block substitution did not happen: replacing an analytic failed mixed endpoint of pi by the intended block endpoint of 0 flips straightening_ratio from -1.000000 to +1.000000 and curvature_slope from +1.5707963268 to -1.5707963268. These are implementation-faithfulness defects; no config, sample-size, or comparability caveat is used to produce this RED.
comparable_reason: Across 4 locally rerun models with the corrected final block, straightening_ratio had Spearman rho -0.258/0.000/+0.894 with d_model/n_layers/vocab_size, while curvature_slope had -0.775/-0.894/0.000; n=4 is too small to call any association intrinsic. There is a direct tokenizer-density mechanism: sampling the same unit-circle path at 6 versus 60 points changed mean curvature from 72.000000 to 6.101695 degrees (-91.53%). The normalized-depth slope also fails a direct twin test: adding 20 exact identity layers to profile [2.1,1.7,1.6,2.0] preserved final state and logits at max error 0.0 but changed curvature_slope from -0.120000 to +0.116000. Matched token boundaries and linguistic spans are required for comparison, but these facts do not alter the implementation verdict.
